description.narrative:
Högnivåmålet för Peace Corridors bidrag med UNDP är att ta itu med utmaningarna relaterade till hållbar mänsklig utveckling och fredsbyggande i Colombia. För att uppnå detta har interventionen tagit hänsyn till två kompletterande tillvägagångssätt: en nationell strategi och en territoriell strategi.
På nationell nivå kommer interventionen: • Stöd UNDP:s Human Development Index Report for Colombia som ett vägledande verktyg för att hantera de viktigaste utvecklingssvårigheterna i landet och främja inkluderande och hållbar ekonomisk tillväxt genom att förbättra kapaciteten hos offentliga institutioner, den privata sektorn och det colombianska civilsamhällets organisationer. • Stöd en av axlarna i fredsavtalet genom att stärka kapaciteten hos återinkorporeringsinstanserna och delegaterna (FARC) som påskyndar genomförandet av ekonomisk och social återanpassning genom interinstitutionell samordning.
På den territoriella nivån - som koncentrerar det mesta av insatsen - kommer bidraget att främja territoriell systemomvandling genom en övergripande strategi för fredsbyggande i tre regioner. Detta tillvägagångssätt kommer att fokuseras på juridisk, socioekonomisk, politisk och miljömässigt hållbar inkludering av de samhällen som har drabbats av konflikter. Målen på territoriell nivå är: • Att öka territoriellt styre, förändra socio-miljömässiga konflikter och orättvisor och skapa social integration och hållbara produktiva alternativ; • Stärka jordbrukarnas kapacitet mot motståndskraft, produktivitet och inkludering för hållbar utveckling som gör det möjligt för dem att övervinna situationer som genereras av efteröverenskommelsen; och, • Förbättra livskvaliteten och utveckla samarbetsrelationer mellan afrocolombianska, ursprungsbefolkade och bondesamhällen (särskilt kvinnor och unga) för att omvandla konflikter genom att få tillgång till formella och korrekta lokala rättssystem, i en demokratisk, pålitlig miljö och med institutioner som kan erbjuda sociala varor och tjänster.

The objective of the project support to UNDP for "Peace Corridors" is to address the challenges related to sustainable Human Development and peace building in Colombia. This is done through two approaches: a national and a territorial.
At the National level, the intervention supports UNDP’s Human Development Index Report for Colombia as a guiding tool to cope with the main development difficulties in the country and promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth by improving the capacities of public institutions, the private sector and Colombian civil society organizations. Peace Corridors also contributes with catalytic actions to strategic positioning in the peace agenda of Colombia and with the progress in compliance with the Peace Agreement.
At the territorial level the contribution will foster Territorial Systemic Transformation through a comprehensive approach of peacebuilding in three regions. This approach will be focused on legal, socio-economic, political, and environmentally sustainable inclusion of the communities that have been affected by conflict.

The high-level objective of the Peace Corridors contribution with UNDP is to address the challenges related to sustainable Human Development and peace building in Colombia. To achieve this, the intervention has taken into consideration two complementary approaches: a national approach and a territorial approach.
At the National level, on the one hand, the intervention will support UNDPs Human Development Index Report for Colombia as a guiding tool to cope with the main development difficulties in the country and promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth by improving the capacities of public institutions, the private sector and Colombian civil society organizations. On the other hand, Peace Corridors will contribute with catalytic actions to strategic positioning in peace agenda of Colombia and with the progress in compliance with the Peace Agreement.
At the territorial level the contribution will foster Territorial Systemic Transformation through a comprehensive approach of peacebuilding in three regions. This approach will be focused on legal, socio-economic, political, and environmentally sustainable inclusion of the communities that have been affected by conflict. The objectives at the territorial level are:
i) To increase territorial governance, transform socio-environmental conflicts and inequities, and generate social inclusion and sustainable productive alternatives;
ii) Strengthen farmer capacities towards resilience, productivity and inclusion for sustainable development that allow them to overcome situations generated by the post-agreement; and,
iii) Improve the quality of life and develop collaborative relationships of Afro-Colombian, indigenous and farmer communities (especially women and young people) to transform conflicts by accessing formal and proper local justice systems, in a democratic, trustworthy environment and with institutions capable of offering social goods and services.

description.narrative:
Some results from 2023 worth highlighting are the following:
Result 1. National level
Result 1.1. Human Development Index Report (INDH) The work with the National Human Development Report represents a collaborative effort that involved multiple stakeholders from the public sector, private sector, and civil society, supported by research from leading Colombian universities.
During 2023, four out of the five so called Human Development "notebooks" were produced and launched on the following subjects (the first one was made end 2022):
Perceptions and Subjective WellBeing in Colombia, launched in March 2023. The report emphasizes the importance of subjective wellbeing indicators beyond traditional metrics. It sheds light on the general public's perceptions regarding their quality of life and happiness, offering insights into the social fabric of Colombia.
Effective Access to Justice for All, a joint launch with the National Planning Department at Universidad Externado de Colombia. This segment explores the challenges in accessing justice across Colombia. Findings indicate that systemic barriers persist, particularly for marginalized groups, but highlight the transformative potential of ensuring equitable access to justice in fostering social cohesion and trust in institutions.
Education: A Driver of Equality, Growth, and Human Development, presented during discussions on higher education reform at Universidad de los Andes. The report underscores education as a fundamental pillar for promoting equality and economic growth. Recommendations for improving the quality of postsecondary education were outlined, indicating a direct link between education quality and social mobility.
Equality and Productivity: Pillars of Human Development in Colombia, launched in partnership with Grupo Prisa, engaging public and private stakeholders. This section presents an analysis of income concentration and its implications for productivity. It argues for inclusive economic policies that address inequality to boost overall economic performance and improve living standards.
The full National Human Development Report was launched in May 2024. A national launch in Bogotá in May was followed by several territorial launches during the rest of the year with presence by the Embassy in the majority of the launches.
Result 1.2. Flexible mechanism for strategic positioning on the peace agenda and support for the national government
This mechanism for supporting the national government's peace policies contributed in 2023 to technical and strategic assistance for the development of key catalytic actions in building and consolidating peace in Colombia.
During 2023 the mechanism focused on two main approaches. The first approach is the strategic support for the Total Peace policy, aimed at promoting strategic and catalytic actions led by the relevant institutions. During the year, among other, strategic support was provided for the consolidation of the technical teams required by the Office of the High Commissioner for Peace (OACP), which contributed to organizing the teams in charge of each ongoing negotiation and dialogue. Additionally, specialized advice on international cooperation was secured, which has contributed to the negotiation process and the international community's support for the peace process initiated under the current government's peace policy.
On the other hand, with the aim of expanding public discussions and deliberations on peace building in Colombia, the Flexible Mechanism supported the forum "The Great National Agreement: The Path to a Comprehensive Peace," held on August 24, 2023. This forum facilitated a conversation with various stakeholders based on the recommendations of the Truth Commission. The forum allowed different voices to exchange experiences and reflections to strengthen the Total Peace initiative led by the president's government.
The second approach involves the Autonomous System of advisory and technical defense for members of the Public Force appearing before the JEP (Special Jurisdiction for Peace), which supports this jurisdiction in achieving its objectives and provides those appearing with more effective tools for supporting justice for the victims of the armed conflict in Colombia, as part of the peace agreement.
During the year guarantees were provided for the participation of 366 Public Force members in 11 meetings across 10 departments of the country. In these meetings, pedagogical tools from the Autonomous Advisory and Defense System for Testimonies (SAAD Comparecientes) were utilized. Among the participants, 3 identified as Indigenous, 4 as AfroColombian, and 15 reported having physical disabilities. This contributed to the development of new pedagogical and educational components and the improvement of existing materials.
In support of the informationsharing strategy led by the Unit for the Search of Disappeared Persons (UBPD), 50 members of the security forces provided information on 113 possible cases of disappearance, which may be relevant for locating missing persons or recovering bodies in Tolima and the Caribbean coast region. These participants have initiated a process of information contribution and follow-up, in compliance with their obligations under the conditionality regime, enabling the support provided for the search for missing persons to be validated by the UBPD and presented to the JEP for sanctioning and benefit acquisition.
Result 2. Territorial level
In 2023, the implementation of the program in the prioritized territories was consolidated. In the MesetasUribe (Meta) corridor, efforts focused on reconciliation through three main components:
Sustainable Tourism: A local tourism council was formed, and seven nature tourism initiatives were launched in Sierra de la Macarena National Park, emphasizing rural women, youth, and Indigenous participation.
Capacity Building for Reconciliation: Community Action Boards adopted reconciliation plans, a youth leadership school promoted peace initiatives, and women leaders were trained to prevent gender based violence.
PLASTIPAZ Initiative: New partnerships for sustainable plastic waste management were established, involving local organizations and peace agreement signatories.
In Northern Cauca corridor, Afro, Indigenous, and peasant communities improved conflict transformation efforts. Key actions included:
Reducing violence through agreements on land titling and promoting productive lines, such as coffee cultivation, in collaboration with ASOCAÑA.
Integrating conflict transformation into local development plans and engaging with election candidates to prioritize peace and conflict management.
These initiatives advanced reconciliation, sustainable development, and conflict resolution across the targeted areas.
Furthermore, for the program as a whole, progress was made in developing communication, gender, and monitoring strategies aimed at strengthening and showcasing the program to potential partners.
